questions.title: Who will succeed Oleksandr Syrskii as Ukraine's top military commander?
questions.background: Oleksandr Syrskii leads Ukraine's armed forces during the war against Russia.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by Ukraine's presidency or reliable contemporaneous reporting, including Al Jazeera. Resolution Condition : Resolve when Ukraine's president formally appoints a successor to Oleksandr Syrskii as the country's top military commander. Temporary or acting appointments do not count unless confirmed as permanent. Accepted Answer Format : The successor's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Zelenskyy's Jan 2026 reshuffle (making Kyrylo Budanov Head of the Presidential Office and Mykhailo Fedorov Defense Minister), Zelenskyy stated he would next turn to resetting the Armed Forces, and June 12 LIGA.net reporting cited a Syrskyi–Fedorov rift over military transformation. Major General Mykhailo Drapatyi (Joint Forces Commander, former Ground Forces Commander) is Ukraine's leading reform-minded battlefield general, closely followed by Chief of the General Staff Andrii Hnatov (the current #2 officer publicly leading June 2026 reform messaging). Pavlo Palisa (Deputy Head of the Presidential Office for military affairs), Ground Forces Commander Hennadii Shapovalov, and Deputy Defense Minister / former Deputy C-in-C Yevhen Moisiuk round out the top five, with 19% reserved for other senior officers.

questions.title: Who will be appointed head of Syria’s National Security Bureau in July 2026?
questions.background: The National Security Bureau oversees Syria’s security agencies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Syrian government announcement or reporting by the Syrian state news agency SANA identifying the person appointed head of the National Security Bureau during July 2026. Resolution Date : The date the appointment is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The appointee’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Syria's Ba'athist National Security Bureau was dissolved after Bashar al-Assad's fall, and President Ahmed al-Sharaa established a National Security Council in March 2025 alongside a restructured General Intelligence Service (initially led by Anas Khattab, who became Interior Minister in spring 2025, and since May 2025 by Hussein al-Salama). If Damascus establishes or revives a National Security Bureau in July 2026 to coordinate security agencies, sitting General Intelligence chief Hussein al-Salama and Interior Minister/former spy chief Anas Khattab (al-Sharaa's top security architect) are the leading internal candidates, followed by Defense Minister Murhaf Abu Qasra, Chief of General Staff Ali Noureddine al-Naasan, and senior presidential/interior insider Ali Keda. Given Damascus's history of elevating lesser-known former HTS security commanders whose full names emerge only upon SANA announcement, a full 50% tail mass is left outside these five figures.

local_articles.title: Syrian-American business forum debuts in Damascus amid push for investment
local_articles.snippet: LONDON: The first Syrian-American Business Forum was held in Damascus on Monday, as the country seeks to rebuild its economic ties with the world and attract foreign investment. Organized by the Ministry of Economy and Industry and the Syrian-American Business Council, the event at the Dama Rose Hotel brought together senior government officials, business leaders and investors. Its aims were to strengthen economic ties by encouraging private-sector partnerships, improve the investment climate and attract international capital for reconstruction and long-term development, the state-run news agency Sana reported Among the dozens of speakers were New York-based international disputes attorney Harout Ekmanian, Syria Report founder Jihad Yazigi and vice president of the Damascus Chamber of Commerce Laila Al-Samman. questions.title: Which European country will declare a national emergency in response to wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements or reliable news reporting published by July 25, 2026. Resolution Condition : Identify the European country whose national government declares a national emergency because of wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026. Regional or local emergency declarations alone do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Europe's late-June 2026 'Omega' heatwave (comparable to 2003) and wet-winter fuel buildup have created extreme early wildfire risk across Southern Europe. Greece is already battling >40C heat and Evia Island evacuations; Portugal has the highest Western European base rate of declaring nationwide wildfire states of alert/calamity and faces firefighter underfunding warnings; Spain has seen a 218% YTD surge in fires (9 large fires vs 1 in 2025) after its worst season on record; and North Macedonia has a strong recent July precedent of declaring formal nationwide wildfire states of crisis (July 2024 and 2025). Italy (16 cities on red alert) takes fifth ahead of smaller tails (Bulgaria, Cyprus, Albania, France, Croatia), with 22% left outside the top five given the strict national-emergency requirement.

local_articles.title: U.K. man describes harrowing escape from Spain wildfire that killed his wife and friends
local_articles.snippet: A British man caught up in Spanish wildfires has described how he survived the inferno as his wife and friends died trying to escape. Malcolm Timbrell, 70, lived with his wife Annette Kilgore, 69, in the village of Bedar, in the Almeria province of southeast Spain. The area was scorched by wildfires on July 9 that killed 13 people, one of the deadliest fires in the country's history. Timbrell spoke to CBS News' partner network BBC News on Monday — outside his blackened, destroyed hillside home — about the ordeal. "You'd never imagine it could happen," he said, "and when it does, and you're the only survivor, then you're left in a situation of, 'What can I do?'" Timbrell and Kilgore moved to Spain after several years sailing together. Having both previously lost partners to terminal illness, they were together for 17 years. questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: July 1-3 data and Fed speeches significantly lowered July 29 rate-hike expectations while highlighting Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack as the most persistent lone-wolf hawk. On July 2, June nonfarm payrolls missed sharply at +57,000 vs. +110,000 consensus alongside -74,000 in downward revisions to April and May (unemployment ticked down to 4.2%, AHE +0.3% MoM / 3.5% YoY), while crude oil fell further to ~$67/bbl from >$90 in early June. CME FedWatch July 29 hike odds dropped from ~30% to ~20%-22% (78%-80% hold), and Chair Kevin Warsh struck a noticeably softer Sintra tone on July 1 noting inflation risks had come down. By contrast, Hammack warned CNBC from Sintra on July 1 that five years of >2% inflation and 'insatiable' AI data-center spending could require higher rates, explicitly contrasting with Warsh's AI-disinflation view. Softer jobs and falling oil reduce both majority-hike odds and the likelihood that labor/oil-sensitive Neel Kashkari or Fed Governor Michelle Bowman dissent in July, boosting solo 'Hammack' (0.09 -> 0.14) and returning solo 'Logan' (0.05) to the top 5 alongside 'Hammack, Logan' (0.14), while trimming 'Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' (0.15 -> 0.11) and 'Bowman, Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' (0.06 -> 0.04) and dropping 'Bowman, Hammack, Logan'. Leaving 52% outside top 5 for a unanimous 12-0 hold, majority-hike coalitions, and other dissent sets ahead of July 8 FOMC minutes and July 14/15 CPI.

questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.

Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Iraq drops sharply 0.40 -> 0.24 because Iraqi Shia militias abstained from the July 7-13 fighting and Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi arrived in Washington on July 13 (through July 18) to meet Trump and sign major US energy deals tied to Baghdad's militia-disarmament pact (though ISW July 10 warns Kataib Hezbollah and Nujaba refuse to disarm, preserving real post-visit retaliation risk). Yemen jumps 0.16 -> 0.23 after Monday July 13's sharpest escalation in years: Yemen's Saudi-backed government struck Sanaa airport to block an Iranian plane, prompting Houthi ballistic missile and drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport and a declaration that de-escalation is over—threatening the 2022 truce and Red Sea shipping just as US-flagged Maersk ships resumed transit (July 9), though JMIC reported no Houthi maritime targeting yet and PLC head al-Alimi sought to cap escalation. Lebanon stays 0.03 (strikes remain Israeli; President Aoun meets Trump July 21) and Syria holds 0.01.

local_articles.title: UN Security Council renews monitoring of Houthi Red Sea attacks amid Yemen airspace escalation
local_articles.snippet: NEW YORK CITY: The UN Security Council on Tuesday adopted a resolution that extends for six months the secretary-general’s mandate to report Houthi attacks against merchant and commercial vessels in the Red Sea. Thirteen of the 15 council members voted in favor of the resolution, while Russia and China abstained. The mandate will now remain in force until Jan. 15, 2027. Resolution 2826, co-authored by the US and Greece, the “penholders” who take the lead on the Red Sea crisis at the Security Council, extends a reporting requirement established under Resolution 2722 in January 2024, and most recently renewed by Resolution 2812 in January this year. The text of the resolution is a straightforward technical rollover, with a single operative paragraph that continues the monitoring mechanism without any substantive changes. local_articles.title: Leading Houthi threatens ‘siege’ on Saudi Arabia after Yemen airport attack
local_articles.snippet: Sanaa, Yemen – A leading official with Yemen’s Houthi rebels, officially known as Ansar Allah, has threatened a “siege” on Saudi Arabia in retaliation for an attack on Sanaa International Airport. The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia for the Monday attack, but Yemen’s internationally recognised government has claimed responsibility, saying that it was a measure to prevent an Iranian plane from landing in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled capital. Speaking to Al Jazeera, Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthi political bureau, said that the group would respond to attacks they perceived to be from Saudi Arabia. questions.title: Which country will the Trump administration target in its first invocation of Section 338 tariff powers by August 18, 2026?
questions.background: Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 authorizes U.S. tariffs in response to discriminatory treatment of American commerce.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country whose exports are targeted by the Trump administration's first invocation of Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, announced on or before August 18, 2026. An announced tariff measure counts even if its effective date has not yet arrived. Use official U.S. announcements or contemporaneous reporting confirming the invocation. Resolution Date : 2026-08-18 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Early July trade developments sharpen Canada's lead as the likeliest discrete Section 338 target ahead of the July 24 expiration of Section 122 global tariffs while easing pressure on France and Brazil: (1) On July 1 the U.S. formally refused to extend USMCA, with USTR Jamieson Greer scheduling talks with Mexico for the week of July 20 while sidelining Canada with no formal USMCA negotiations (Straits Times July 1, Al Jazeera July 6), and Canada was previously excluded from March 11 Section 301 probes — leaving Section 338 uniquely relevant for bilateral discrimination disputes; (2) On July 1 the EU eliminated tariffs on U.S. industrial imports under the EU-U.S. Joint Statement (Benzinga July 3), de-escalating immediate transatlantic friction and trimming France (0.09 -> 0.06); (3) On July 6 Flavio Bolsonaro lobbied USTR to delay the June-proposed 25% Section 301 Brazil tariff by 180 days until after October's election (Straits Times/Al Jazeera July 6), modestly trimming Brazil (0.12 -> 0.10); (4) July 7-11 USTR Section 301 forced-labor hearings proposing 12.5% tariffs across 46/60 economies (including India, China, South Korea, Japan) provide the primary tariff vehicle for Asia, while India also signed a $1.8M lobbying deal with Trump-aligned firm (HT July 7). Raising Canada (0.18 -> 0.24), holding China (0.15) and India (0.08), and retaining 37% tail mass outside the top 5 (Mexico, UK, South Korea, Japan, Germany, Vietnam, etc.) reflects the lack of an explicit Section 338 target announcement so far.
